bindings.caption: Combine 0.3 mmol InI3, 0.5 equivalent EDTA and 5 mL anhydrous oleylamine in a 50 mL three-neck flask. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.

bindings.caption: Hold the precursor mixture under vacuum at 120 °C for 1 h. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Replace vacuum with an inert atmosphere and heat to 180 °C. Nitrogen glovebox or Schlenk handling is stated generally. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main p.7 synthesis; SI p.14 Figure S15

bindings.caption: Rapidly inject 0.33 mL (1.2 mmol) tris(diethylamino)phosphine. Exact injection duration is unreported. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main PDF p.7 / printed 6158, General Considerations and Synthesis of InP Quantum Dots

bindings.caption: Monitor until the absorption spectrum is constant; reported after 30 min. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.
bindings.source_locator: Main p.7 synthesis; SI p.14 Figure S15

bindings.caption: Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature and move it into a nitrogen glovebox. Conceptual operation diagram; only source-stated equipment and conditions apply.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
